record.summary: Bill for an organic law to regulate and promote AI in Ecuador, filed by assembly member Patricia Núñez in June 2024. It sorted AI systems into four risk levels and banned extreme-risk practices such as mass social scoring, imperceptible manipulation, lethal autonomous weapons and indiscriminate surveillance. High-risk systems were to be registered and to ensure explainability, meaningful human oversight, unbiased data, cybersecurity and audit trails, with prior human rights impact assessments; people gained rights against solely automated decisions, and AI-generated works had to be labelled. The Plenary archived it on 15 Sep 2026.
record.notes: Filed on 20 Jun 2024 with 83 articles and qualified by the Legislative Administration Council on 26 Jul 2024 (CAL-HKK-2023-2025-0376). On 31 Aug 2026 the Committee on Education, Culture, Science, Technology, Innovation and Ancestral Knowledge approved, with seven votes, a first-debate report recommending archiving. It cited the lack of adaptive governance tools (national guidelines, technical standards, sectoral rules, codes of conduct, transparency standards and impact assessments for high-risk systems), new spending for the powers given to the telecommunications ministry (MINTEL) and the personal data protection superintendency (SPDP), contrary to Article 135 of the Constitution, a sanctions regime that left the ranges and limits of penalties to the regulation, the risk of early over-regulation, and overlap with the Organic Law on Personal Data Protection and the Organic Law for Digital and Audiovisual Transformation; it pointed to ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI as international references. The Plenary approved the archiving in first debate with 88 votes on 15 Sep 2026. The committee chair, Cecilia Baltazar, said the archiving does not set AI regulation aside but means first building the institutional, technical and legal conditions for an updated framework, and the report calls for first strengthening the national strategy for the ethical and responsible development and use of AI.

summary.quote: La legisladora por la provincia de Chimborazo, Patricia Núñez presentó una nueva iniciativa legal
Los sistemas de IA se clasificarán en cuatro niveles de riesgo
Sistemas de calificación social masiva que categoricen y determinen castigos
Armas autónomas letales o sistemas automatizados de uso de la fuerza contra seres humanos
Tecnologías de vigilancia indiscriminada o predictiva que intercedan masivamente comunicaciones privadas
deberán inscribirlos en el Registro Nacional de Sistemas de IA de Alto Riesgo, antes de su puesta en operación
Asegurar la intervención y supervisión humana significativa en las decisiones que puedan afectar sustancialmente los derechos
Implementar mecanismos de trazabilidad y registro inalterable de las operaciones realizadas
deberán realizar una evaluación de impacto en los derechos humanos (EIDH) de manera previa a su desarrollo, despliegue o uso sustancial
Toda persona tiene derecho a no ser objeto de una decisión basada únicamente en el tratamiento automatizado de sus datos personales
Obligación de etiquetado de productos generados por IA
